text: Why do my legs hurt two days after squats?

steps.title: Example: the squat session
steps.say: As an example, I put a squat session two days ago. Heavy lifting strains quad fibres, especially while they lengthen under load, and causes tiny tears.

steps.title: Hours later: cleanup crew
steps.say: Immune cells gather at the tears and fluid seeps in. This repair work is what swells the muscle, and it takes a day or so to build.

steps.title: Two days on: peak soreness
steps.say: By now swelling and the repair chemicals are irritating pain nerves, so you may feel the ache most today. Rebuilding then leaves fibres a bit stronger.

lines.text: Squats cause tiny tears in your quad fibres, and the repair work causes the ache.
Immune cells and fluid irritate pain nerves, so soreness peaks around day two.
You may feel it ease over the next couple of days as fibres rebuild stronger.
